solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jewish leader, a divine involved in returning ark from the north

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word for the chest is read right to left
to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a kist is a Scots and northern English word for a chest or ark
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a crossword divine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rabbi and a cleric bring the Ark of the Covenant back from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed chest TSIK is split around A plus DD to give TS-ADD-IK.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsaddik is a righteous man, a title for a revered Hasidic spiritual leader.

clue.text: Two heartlessly throw rubbish

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: the number word
to throw or toss, as at a coconut stall at a fair

explanation.surface: A pair of people callously chuck away the garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'rubbish' is an adjective, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Toshy means trashy or worthless, the adjective formed from tosh, meaning nonsense.

clue.text: Gangrene developed in a chap's large toe

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's big toe has turned gangrenous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed in' reads as one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sphacelation is the medical term for mortification of tissue, that is the formation of gangrene.

clue.text: Eccentric American Democrat's appeal over second year

parts.note: D stands for a Democrat in US politics
it means sex appeal
S is the abbreviation for second
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An oddball US politician lodges an appeal concerning a sophomore.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the appeal above the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditsy is informal for scatterbrained or silly, a fair match for eccentric behaviour.

clue.text: Growth of international law

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for international
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: The development of international law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' means a plant, not development.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the holly genus, and a plant is something that grows.

clue.text: Burmese native jackdaw seen over rising interior

parts.note: ka or kae is a Scots word for a jackdaw

indicators.note: in a down clue something rising is read from the bottom up

parts.note: inner means interior

explanation.surface: A local in Burma watches a jackdaw fly up over the hinterland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Karenni are a people of eastern Burma, also called the Red Karen.

clue.text: Scruffy Australian beginning on grade A hemp

parts.note: in Australian slang a dag is a scruffy or unfashionable person

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of grade
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishevelled Aussie starts on top-quality cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagga is the South African name for cannabis, a kind of hemp smoked as a drug.

clue.text: Declare once? Declare twice to make it!

parts.note: the word written out twice in a row

explanation.surface: An instruction-like quip: say it once, then say it twice to get there.
explanation.walkthrough: Write DECLAREDECLARE and take the letters across the join, declARE DEclare, dropping the rest; the setter reuses the definition's word on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Arede is an archaic, Spenserian form of aread, meaning to declare or explain; 'once' marks it as old.

clue.text: Searches the internet about current deceptive questions

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to google is to search the web
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone browses the web for trick questions on topical matters.
explanation.walkthrough: A googly is a cricket ball that breaks the opposite way to the one the batter expects, hence any tricky question.
explanation.definitionFit: A googly in cricket deceives the batter, so figuratively it is a tricky, misleading question.

clue.text: Fibrous connection unfortunately uncurable in mouth tissue

indicators.note: in places the rearranged word inside the tissue word

parts.note: the gum is the tissue around the teeth

indicators.note: something going unfortunately goes wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor diagnoses an incurable growth in the gums.
explanation.definitionFit: The gubernaculum is a fibrous cord in the embryo, notably the ligament guiding the testis or a developing tooth.

clue.text: All at once a Nile hazard on Egyptian banks

parts.note: taken as written
the sudd is a mass of floating vegetation blocking the White Nile

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its two edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of Egyptian

explanation.surface: Suddenly a navigational danger looms on the banks of the river in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: The sudd is a vast swamp of floating plants in South Sudan.
explanation.definitionFit: Asudden is an old adverb meaning suddenly, that is all at once.

clue.text: Pastor in US state, our last freely worshipping snakes

indicators.note: in places the clergyman's letter inside the name of the state

parts.note: a state of the USA
P is an abbreviation for pastor

indicators.note: used freely, the letters are released from their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman in Ohio last of all handles snakes in worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pastor' looks like a whole word to place, but it supplies only its abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophiolatry is serpent worship, from Greek ophis, snake, so ophiolatrous means given to it.

clue.text: Brittle star they found swimming

indicators.note: things swimming move about freely, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Divers spot a brittle star in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brittle star' looks like one phrase, a sea creature; the definition is 'Brittle' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattery describes something that shatters easily, which is what brittle means.

clue.text: Wagon, good one on the tube

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits beneath it, so the first-named pair goes second

parts.note: the tube is slang for television, the tele
G is the abbreviation for good
a means one

explanation.surface: A decent wagon was spotted on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tube' suggests the London Underground but means television; in a down clue 'on' puts the second part below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A telega is a rough four-wheeled Russian cart, a kind of wagon.

clue.text: Greet old artist before exhibition's opening

parts.note: Frans Hals was a seventeenth-century Dutch painter

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of exhibition

explanation.surface: Welcome an Old Master before the show opens.
explanation.definitionFit: Halse is an old word meaning to embrace or salute, so to greet someone.

clue.text: With borders guarded, hard to leave

indicators.note: the letter told to leave is removed from the word

parts.note: hedged means protected or guarded
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A country with closely guarded frontiers is hard to get out of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edged has edges, that is it is bordered or trimmed.

clue.text: Open land regularly seen in Chad map? Bang on, lad!

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters

explanation.surface: Someone praises a lad's map of the African country Chad as spot on.
explanation.definitionFit: A campagna is a flat open plain, from the Italian, as in the Roman Campagna.

clue.text: Shoemaker's thread left inside on backing

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
in means inside

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the cricket word is read right to left

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A cobbler's thread has been left inside, stuck onto the backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingel is an old word for a waxed thread used by shoemakers.

clue.text: Girl initially runs in without foundation garment

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word

parts.note: the first letter of girl

indicators.note: in places the cricket abbreviation inside the other word

parts.note: idle talk is baseless, without foundation
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A girl first goes out without her corset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundation garment' reads as one phrase, a corset, which a girdle is; the definition is 'garment' and 'without foundation' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle is a close-fitting elastic undergarment, a piece of clothing.

clue.text: Actor losing a new amulet

indicators.note: losing means the named letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: Sean Bean is an English actor
a single N, the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A performer has lost a brand-new lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea bean is a drifted seed, often worn or carried as a good-luck charm.

clue.text: Sort of bird, millions in aeries all over the place

indicators.note: letters all over the place are scattered into a new order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for millions
taken as written

explanation.surface: Millions of birds nest in eyries everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The seriema is a long-legged South American ground bird.

clue.text: Accountant is sorry for falls due

parts.note: ACC is an abbreviation for accountant
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: An accountant apologises for overdue payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is sorry for' looks like one phrase; 'for' is just the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest accrues when it builds up and becomes payable, that is falls due.

clue.text: Flexible stem denying aquilegia a lot of support

indicators.note: denying the flower something means withholding letters from it

parts.note: aquilegia is the botanical name for the columbine
most of the word column, a pillar

explanation.surface: A floppy stem that cannot hold up a heavy flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bine is the twining climbing stem of a plant such as hop, flexible by nature.

clue.text: See both sides of motorway covered in trees

indicators.note: being on both sides of something means surrounding it

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is one in Cambridgeshire
M for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Look at the motorway with woods on both verges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a command to look, but is a church diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmy means full of or covered with elm trees.

clue.text: Magical figure shedding luminance, article of a sorceress

indicators.note: shedding something means dropping it, so a letter falls out

parts.note: a magic circle is the figure a magician draws
L is the symbol for luminance
an indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wizardly figure dims, revealing a witch's object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magical' wants to be the definition, but it goes with figure; the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Circean means relating to Circe, the enchantress of the Odyssey who turned men into swine.

clue.text: Source of legumes it's said go with fish

indicators.note: what is said is heard, so the word is spelt as another that sounds the same

parts.note: go is a euphemism for urinate
a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A recipe note: legumes go well with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go with' reads as 'accompany'; 'go' means relieve oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A peacod is an old word for a pea pod, which holds the peas.

clue.text: Tricky rock worked in Cornwall

definitions.meaning: first meaning: elvish, mischievous like an elf
second meaning: a Cornish name for a quarried igneous rock

explanation.surface: A hard-to-handle stone quarried in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Elvan is a Cornish quarryman's word for quartz-porphyry dyke rock; as an old adjective it means elfish, hence mischievous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an obsolete adjective for elfish mischief, and a Cornish name for a granitic dyke rock.

clue.text: Farm implement Chinese used in water

indicators.note: used in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: wet as a noun means water or moisture
CH is an abbreviation for Chinese

explanation.surface: A Chinese tool for the fields is used in irrigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A wecht is a Scots term for a hoop-like tray used to winnow or carry grain on the farm.

clue.text: Audibly express admiration of green stone

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the answer sounds like the phrase's word

parts.note: to praise is to express admiration

explanation.surface: Say out loud how much you admire an emerald.
explanation.definitionFit: Prase is a leek-green variety of chalcedony quartz, a green stone.

clue.text: Version of Bible partly reordered Galatians

indicators.note: here reordered means put in the opposite order, read backwards
partly means only part of the word is used, a run of its letters

parts.note: a run of letters from inside the word

explanation.surface: A Bible edition with part of Paul's letter to the Galatians rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reordered' could suggest an anagram, but the hidden run is simply reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Itala is an early Latin translation of the Bible, predating Jerome's Vulgate.

clue.text: Warrant earlier festival once about Britain

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: an ale was formerly a village festival with drinking, as in church-ale
B is an abbreviation for Britain

explanation.surface: A warrant was once issued for a festival concerning Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' and 'once' each mark an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare able is a verb meaning to vouch for or guarantee, that is to warrant.

clue.text: Ghost of deceased spirit returns after having drained Lethe

indicators.note: a drained word is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the outside letters of Lethe

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the drink is read right to left

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A dead man's ghost comes back having drunk from Lethe, the underworld river of forgetting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethe is the river of oblivion in Hades, a fitting surface for a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman religion the lemures were restless spirits of the dead; the singular is lemur.

clue.text: A fish cake sent back — rather milky nature?

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
luce is an old name for the pike
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A diner returns a fish cake, finding it rather milky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milky' hints at the Milky Way: the Nubeculae are the Magellanic Clouds; the word also means a cloudiness in urine or the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubecula means a little cloud, a slight cloudiness, which is a rather milky appearance.

clue.text: Like flowers of hibiscus, hybrid should open AM

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross of parts, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hybrid hibiscus's flowers should open in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid' fits the gardening scene but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Monadelphous flowers have stamens united into one bundle by their filaments, as in mallows like hibiscus.

clue.text: A novel type of fruit

parts.note: taken as written
Nana is a novel by Emile Zola

explanation.surface: A new variety of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as new but names a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Anana is an old name for the pineapple, a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Position for fencing division I note

parts.note: a sept is a division of a clan
taken as written
me, also mi, is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A farmer notes the part of a field fixed for putting up fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests putting up fences, but it is the sword sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Septime is the seventh of the classical parrying positions in sword fencing.
